epics.title: Content-Hash Document Upload Deduplication & Legacy Duplicate Consolidation
epics.jtbd: When an educational administrator uploads an administrative PDF or DOCX document to the CRIE portal, I want the system to detect identical content via SHA-256 hash and consolidate legacy duplicate rows without losing extracted records, so that duplicate document entries never pollute the SQLite registry and I can immediately review or update previously extracted data.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: 0% duplicate document creation rate on identical re-uploads and 100% foreign-key preservation across merged IDs 1, 10, and 11
epics.tocConstraintRef: Lack of deterministic content-hash constraint and legacy duplicate rows ID 1, 10, 11 splitting child records
requirements: R1: Add a content_sha256 column plus normalized filename and extracted-text-size fallback metadata with a lookup index to the SQLite documents table in crie_document_engine.py, computed deterministically during ingestion.

R2: Implement deterministic duplicate resolution in crie_document_engine.py so any upload matching an existing content_sha256 (or normalized filename and extracted-text-size fallback for legacy rows) prevents inserting a new document row and resolves the canonical existing document ID.

R3: Update the upload endpoint in crie_assistant_api.py to return deduplicated=true, the canonical existing document_id, the list of already-extracted structured records (enrolled_trainees, pps_staff, rup_curricula), and a clear prompt/action to review or correct existing records when a duplicate is uploaded.

R4: Handle empty, corrupted, or unsupported uploads and storage/hash errors with explicit structured HTTP 4xx/5xx error responses without creating orphan document rows or discarding user upload context.

R5: Provide an idempotent, transactional SQLite migration and cleanup script (scripts/merge_duplicate_documents.py) that merges existing duplicate documents ID 1, 10, and 11 into one canonical record, backfills content_sha256, and remaps all child foreign keys without data loss.

R6: Surface deduplicated upload feedback in the web upload interface so users clearly see that the document already exists, inspect its extracted records, and transition into record correction rather than retrying blindly.

R7: Verify hash calculation, duplicate interception, legacy ID 1/10/11 merge idempotency, and upload endpoint response shape (deduplicated=true and original document ID) across unit, integration, and E2E tests.

Given the migration script has already run once, When it is executed a second time, Then it completes idempotently with zero errors and zero record loss.
Given a document uploaded via crie_document_engine.py, When its byte stream is ingested, Then content_sha256 and normalized filename plus text-size metadata are persisted and indexed.
slices.tocConstraintRef: Foreign-key remapping across legacy documents 1, 10, 11 during schema migration
slices.sixSigmaMetric: 100% foreign-key referential integrity after migration with 0 orphaned child records

epics.title: Interactive Structured Registry CRUD, Chat Correction Tools & Revision Audit
epics.jtbd: When an educational administrator uploads or selects a document in the CRIE portal, I want to inspect extracted enrolled_trainees, pps_staff, and rup_curricula records and correct individual fields via UI or chat commands with full revision logging, so that SQLite always holds verified institutional data reflected immediately in assistant responses.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: 100% of validated field corrections persisted atomically with revision audit entries and reflected in the very next assistant response
epics.tocConstraintRef: Read-only extracted SQLite tables lacking typed CRUD mutations, agent update tools, and prompt cache invalidation
requirements: R1: Create a SQLite registry_revisions audit table and transactional CRUD persistence methods in crie_persistent_memory.py for reading, updating, and confirming safe deletion of rows in enrolled_trainees, pps_staff, and rup_curricula scoped by document_id.

R2: Enforce strict domain validation on record updates (non-empty full name, valid specialty code, valid study/funding basis, valid pps_staff binding, non-negative rup_curricula hours) and record before/after values, actor, timestamp, and reason in registry_revisions.
R3: Expose REST endpoints in crie_assistant_api.py to list structured records linked to any document ID (including IDs 1-11), apply targeted field updates, and retrieve revision history.

R4: Implement agent tools in crie_autonomous_agent.py and crie_smart_consultant.py that display a structured card of records extracted from an uploaded or selected document and execute natural-language correction commands directly against SQLite.

R5: Ensure subsequent assistant turns query live SQLite state from crie_persistent_memory.py and invalidate any stale cached context so corrected trainee, faculty, or curriculum values appear immediately in the next answer.

R6: Build responsive UI record cards and inline editing controls in the web interface so administrators can inspect extracted records, edit fields, confirm destructive removals, and view update confirmation on desktop and mobile.
R7: Return clear validation and persistence error feedback in both REST and chat responses without mutating SQLite or discarding user-entered edits when validation or network errors occur.
R8: Verify SQLite revision logging, REST CRUD endpoints, chat-driven record correction on document IDs 1-11, and immediate next-turn assistant grounding via unit, SQL integration, and E2E tests.

epics.title: Document Lifecycle, Deduplication & Registry Correction Telemetry (GQM)
epics.jtbd: When operating the CRIE document upload, deduplication, and interactive registry correction workflows, I want Goal-Question-Metric telemetry measuring Goal: enabling administrators to maintain a duplicate-free, accurate SQLite registry without manual SQL fixes or jargon confusion by answering Q1 (are duplicate uploads intercepted without creating redundant rows?), Q2 (do record corrections succeed with revision audit and immediate next-turn reflection?), and Q3 (do upload/edit help questions receive jargon-free DB-grounded guidance?), so that operational effectiveness is objectively verified.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: 100% GQM metric coverage answering Q1-Q3 with zero unrequested counter bloat
epics.tocConstraintRef: Lack of structured event instrumentation linking upload deduplication, record edits, and help compliance to outcomes
requirements: R1: State the GQM Goal (duplicate-free, self-service accurate structured registry without jargon confusion) and Questions Q1 (duplicate upload interception), Q2 (validated record correction & freshness), and Q3 (jargon-free live guidance compliance) in telemetry schemas and storage.

R2: Record lightweight GQM events in SQLite/telemetry storage solely for Q1 (deduplicated vs new upload counts), Q2 (correction attempts, validation rejections, revision writes, and post-edit query hits), and Q3 (upload-help queries checked against the banned-jargon filter).
R3: Expose a concise GQM summary endpoint in crie_assistant_api.py computing only the derived rates answering Q1, Q2, and Q3.
R4: Ensure telemetry instrumentation fails open without blocking primary upload, correction, or chat paths if metric logging encounters an error.
R5: Verify GQM metric derivations and non-blocking event capture with unit and API integration tests.

epics.title: Live DB Registry Guidance & Prompt-Jargon Elimination
epics.jtbd: When an educational administrator asks the CRIE assistant how to upload, edit, or use files to correct institutional data, I want the assistant to omit internal prompt-engineering jargon and respond with live SQLite document statistics plus clear step-by-step UI instructions, so that users immediately understand what data is already loaded and how to update it.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: 0% occurrence of banned prompt-engineering jargon (such as 'slot' or 'system prompt') and 100% alignment with live SQLite document/table counts
epics.tocConstraintRef: Hardcoded prompt-engineering terminology in consultant/agent prompts masking live DB registry state
requirements: R1: Audit and remove all internal prompt-engineering terminology (including 'slot to current reply', 'system prompt', 'context slot', and their Russian equivalents) from crie_smart_consultant.py, crie_thought_agent.py, and crie_autonomous_agent.py prompts and response templates.

R2: Implement a live SQLite registry-summary query helper returning actual uploaded document titles/IDs (such as residency and postgraduate admission orders) and exact extracted record counts across enrolled_trainees, pps_staff, and rup_curricula (plus a clear empty-state fallback when no documents are loaded).

R3: Route user questions about uploading, editing, or managing files through a live-grounded guidance builder in crie_smart_consultant.py, crie_thought_agent.py, and crie_autonomous_agent.py that cites real uploaded documents, per-table record counts, and step-by-step UI instructions (attach file button -> automatic DB parsing -> review and edit fields in chat or table).

R4: Add a deterministic output guardrail/sanitizer in the consultant and agent response pipeline that detects and strips or rewrites any forbidden prompt-engineering jargon before sending replies to the client.
R5: Ensure the chat endpoint in crie_assistant_api.py cleanly forwards upload/editing help intents through the jargon-free live-registry pipeline with consistent structured error handling.

R6: Verify across unit and chat integration tests that asking 'how do I send you files to correct data?' (including the Russian prompt equivalent) never contains 'slot' or prompt jargon and accurately reports live DB document statistics and editing steps.
